Temporal shot timing (primitive 3) captures the critical 0–7 second window post-possession change, aligning with high-success counter-attack scenarios. These primitives form a dual framework: one spatially grounded in player occupation, the other temporally anchored in game flow. Failure modes include misclassification due to noisy SportVU data or violation of assumptions (e.g., dribble detection errors). Dualities emerge in how spatial dominance correlates with shot timing—high-value shots often occur when defensive zones are least defined. The models assume deterministic player motion and static opponent positions, which may fail under high-intensity defensive pressure or erratic movement patterns.
